name: Low-volatility regime momentum (1h)
rationale: Momentum pays best in CALM regimes: when realized volatility is below a ceiling, a positive medium return reflects orderly trend accumulation rather than a violent, revert-prone spike. Gating momentum on low vol harvests the smooth drift while sitting out the whipsaw of high-vol regimes. The other side is the fader who shorts a quiet uptrend that just keeps grinding. Edge persists because low-vol trends have high signal-to-noise and are under-chased. Distinct from all breakout specs: this AVOIDS volatility rather than requiring it. Disconfirmer: exits when the return flips negative or realized vol spikes past the regime bound (regime changed) — captured by the signal exit — else the stop fires.
catalyst: orderly positive drift in a low-volatility regime
